errors.evidence: The x-axis does not have a standard logarithmic scale; the tick marks are at custom, non-uniform intervals (1e7, 2e7, 5e7, 1e8, etc.), which is not a true logarithmic progression.

errors.text_span: a relatively stable loss ratio around 99.8% across all TFLOP values
errors.evidence: The Vanilla model (purple line) has a constant loss ratio of exactly 100%, not 99.8%.
The SepLLM (n=64) model is represented by an orange line with plus-like or vertical line markers, not square markers.
For the SepLLM (n=64) model, the loss ratio at 9e8 TFLOPs is approximately 100%, not 99.8%.
The SepLLM (n=128) model is depicted with cross (x-shaped) markers, not star markers.
The SepLLM (n=64, H) model (green line) peaks at 6e8 TFLOPs, not 5e8 TFLOPs.

errors.text_span: with a peak around 99.2% at 3e8 TFLOPs
errors.evidence: The SepLLM (n=64, H/T) model (red line) peaks at 4e8 TFLOPs with a value of approximately 99.1%, not at 3e8 TFLOPs with a value of 99.2%.

errors.text_span: All models exhibit an increasing trend in loss ratio as the number of TFLOPs increases
errors.evidence: This is an incorrect generalization. The Vanilla model has a flat trend (0% increase), and several other models (e.g., SepLLM n=128, n=64 H, and n=64 H/T) show a slight decrease after reaching a peak.

errors.text_span: with the SepLLM (n=64, H) model showing the highest loss ratio across most TFLOP values
errors.evidence: This statement is false. The Vanilla model has the highest loss ratio (100%) across all TFLOPs. Among the other models, the SepLLM (n=64) model (orange line) has the highest ratio for most of the range from ~1.5e8 TFLOPs onwards.
